summary: Yuan Ren is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Phyllis Granoff.

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Gongga Rinpoche. He held posts as a researcher at the Chinese Buddhist Culture Research Institute and at the Jinling Sutra Publishing House.

Yudru Tsomu is a historian and Tibetologist who earned a PhD at Harvard University. She studied under Leonard van der Kuijp, Mark C. Elliott, Janet Gyatso, Philip A. Kuhn, James E. Bosson, and Wesley M. Jacobsen.
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He founded Huayan University and served as a teacher there.

Yuguang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University circa 1965–1974 and later served as the university's president (学長) circa 2013–2015.

Yui Suzuki specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She studied at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna. He held professorships at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) studied at Bukkyo and Doshisha Universities in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Bukkyo University (~1956–1997), Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen (~1997–2010), Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, Shōjōke-in Temple (~1999–2008), and Chion-in Temple (~2010–2020).

Yujun Endo (1939–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He spent his career at Taisho University, where he served as an associate professor (attested 1991) and later professor emeritus (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2015, she was attested as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Ryukoku University and Hanazono University.

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku and Kyushu Universities, held a post at Shuchiin University, and served at Koyasan University as director (~1961–1999), professor, president, and professor emeritus.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and was later a part-time lecturer there (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn, later serving as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura and Daito Shimaji, and later held posts at Toyo University (~1949–1962) and as president of Rissho University (~1968–1973).

Yukio Yamanaka is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He was a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and later served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

Yuko Kamishima (born 1971) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo and as a research student under Ekai Kawaguchi, and later held a post at Ritsumeikan University.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held an academic post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and Katsuhiko Kamimura and earned a PhD from the University of Groningen. She served as associate professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2012–2021) at Kyoto University.
